source_results.title: Hormesis in Aging and Neurodegeneration—A Prodigy Awaiting Dissection

concepts.mechanism_summary: Hormesis is a biphasic dose-response relationship in which low-dose exposures produce stimulatory or beneficial effects while high-dose exposures are inhibitory or toxic, characterised by a U-shaped or inverted-U-shaped curve. It is 'an adaptive mechanism of a cell or an organism to compensate for any disruption in homeostasis caused by exposure to mild stresses' — the low-dose exposure preconditions the cell by activating stress-resistance pathways (e.g., heat-shock proteins, DNA repair enzymes, xenobiotic detoxification), increasing maintenance and repair capacity. The magnitude of the low-dose stimulatory effect is typically 30–60% above control, and the response is evolutionarily conserved.

atoms.verbatim_quote: exposure to mild levels of harmful factors preconditions a cell or an organism in that it stimulates the activation of stress resistance mechanisms, thus fostering the cellular capacity of maintenance and repair
atoms.mechanism_atom: Low-dose stressor induces activation of stress-resistance pathways, increasing repair capacity as a protective preconditioning response

atoms.verbatim_quote: Hormesis describes an evolutionarily conserved process by which a cell or an entire organism can be preconditioned, meaning that previous exposure to low doses of an insult protects against a higher, normally harmful or lethal dose of the same stressor
atoms.mechanism_atom: Prior low-dose insult transforms cellular vulnerability into resistance, so that subsequent high-dose exposure causes less harm (cross-tolerance)

atoms.verbatim_quote: Hormesis is characterized by the U-shaped (or inverted U-shaped) response of a system to different values of the stressor, meaning the system shows different inhibitory or stimulatory behavior when exposed to low or high doses of the stressor
atoms.mechanism_atom: The biphasic dose-response produces a non-monotonic curve where low doses stimulate and high doses inhibit, yielding a quantifiable overcompensation zone

concepts.mechanism_summary: Leukocyte extravasation is 'the passage of cells through the intact vessel wall and the movement of white blood cells out of the circulatory system towards the site of tissue damage or infection', occurring mainly in post-capillary venules. The cascade proceeds: tethering/rolling (selectin-mediated), chemokine-triggered activation, firm arrest (integrin–ICAM binding), intravascular crawling, then transmigration through endothelial junctions (paracellular, PECAM-dependent) or through the cell body (transcellular). Once through the endothelium, leukocytes penetrate the basement membrane via proteolysis and/or mechanical force.

source_results.title: Referred Pain - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
Referred pain: characteristics, possible mechanisms, and clinical management

concepts.mechanism_summary: Referred pain is 'pain perceived as arising in a region of the body innervated by nerves other than those that innervate the actual source of pain.' The dominant explanatory mechanism is convergence-projection theory: visceral and somatic afferent fibers converge onto the same dorsal horn spinothalamic neurons, so the brain cannot correctly identify the origin of the signal and projects pain to the somatic (surface) territory sharing that spinal level. A second mechanism — central hyperexcitability — holds that 'new receptive fields are created as a result of the opening of latent convergent afferent fibers in the dorsal horn,' expanding referred pain area with increased stimulus intensity or chronicity.

atoms.verbatim_quote: Nerves from visceral and somatic structures enter the central nervous system at the same level and converge on the same spinothalamic neurons
atoms.mechanism_atom: Convergent visceral and somatic afferents propagate signals onto shared dorsal horn neurons, causing higher centers to misattribute visceral pain to the somatic territory

atoms.verbatim_quote: new receptive fields are created as a result of the opening of latent convergent afferent fibers in the dorsal horn, and this signal could then be perceived as referred pain
atoms.mechanism_atom: Persistent nociceptive input activates previously silent (latent) convergent fibers in the dorsal horn, creating new receptive fields and expanding referred pain area

atoms.verbatim_quote: temporal summation is a potent mechanism for generation of referred muscle pain, and central hyperexcitability is important for the extent of referred pain
atoms.mechanism_atom: Repeated subthreshold nociceptive impulses accumulate via temporal summation to build central hyperexcitability, determining how far referred pain spreads

Eustachian tube pressure equilibration. Temporal analysis of pressure changes based on direct physiological recordings

concepts.mechanism_summary: The Eustachian tube is normally closed and passively sealed against the nasopharynx. 'Yawning and swallowing cause contraction of the muscles connected to the Eustachian tube, enabling the tube to open to small amounts of air, which allows for the equalization of pressure between the atmosphere and the middle ear.' Specifically, the tensor veli palatini muscle 'contracts the anterolateral wall to cause dilation and opening of the distal Eustachian tube' while the levator veli palatini elevates the cartilaginous floor; together they transiently open the lumen to allow gas exchange. The tube then passively re-closes, maintaining a pressure-equalized middle ear cavity essential for normal tympanic membrane vibration.

atoms.mechanism_atom: Muscle contraction transiently opens the tube to exchange small air volumes between nasopharynx and middle ear, equalizing pressure differentials

atoms.verbatim_quote: The tensor veli palatini muscle is a thin, triangular muscle of the head that tenses the soft palate and opens the Eustachian tube to equalise pressure in the middle ear
atoms.mechanism_atom: The tensor veli palatini muscle regulates Eustachian tube lumen diameter by dilating the anterolateral wall on contraction, gating pressure equalization

atoms.verbatim_quote: on descent, the volume of air in the middle ear shrinks and a slight vacuum is produced, requiring active opening of the Eustachian tube (through actions like swallowing or the Valsalva maneuver) to equalize the pressure
atoms.mechanism_atom: A pressure differential accumulates across the tympanic membrane as ambient pressure changes, requiring active muscular gating to discharge the vacuum and restore equilibrium

concepts.mechanism_summary: A tuned mass damper is 'a device mounted in structures to reduce mechanical vibrations, consisting of a mass mounted on one or more damped springs.' Its core mechanism: 'Its oscillation frequency is tuned to be similar to the resonant frequency of the object it is mounted to,' causing the TMD mass to 'vibrate one hundred eighty degrees (180°) out of phase with the vibrating structure.' Consequently, 'the tuned mass damper essentially absorbs a substantial portion of the energy of the vibrating structure and cancels the structure motion at the predetermined frequency.' The ideal phase difference of 90 degrees at the target frequency achieves maximum energy transfer from structure to damper.

source_results.title: Cathodic corrosion protection with sacrificial anodes
How Cathodic Protection and Sacrificial Anodes Prevent Rusting

concepts.mechanism_summary: Cathodic protection makes the metal to be protected the cathode of an electrochemical cell by connecting it to a more electrochemically active metal (the sacrificial anode). 'The sacrificial metal then corrodes instead of the protected metal.' Specifically, 'these anodes are made from a metal alloy with a more active voltage than the metal of the structure, and the difference in potential causes the galvanic anode to corrode, protecting the structure.' The more negative reduction potential of the anode (zinc, magnesium, or aluminium) drives spontaneous electron flow to the protected cathode, suppressing oxidation reactions at the cathode surface by maintaining it in a reduced electrochemical state.

atoms.verbatim_quote: The sacrificial metal then corrodes instead of the protected metal
atoms.mechanism_atom: Preferential oxidation of the sacrificial anode inhibits corrosion of the protected cathode by diverting the oxidation reaction to the more active metal

atoms.verbatim_quote: the difference in potential causes the galvanic anode to corrode, protecting the structure
atoms.mechanism_atom: The electrochemical potential difference between anode and cathode produces spontaneous electron flow that keeps the protected structure in a cathodic (non-corroding) state

atoms.verbatim_quote: Sacrificial anodes are made from metals with a more negative electrochemical potential than the metal they're protecting, so they preferentially oxidize
atoms.mechanism_atom: The anode material preferentially accumulates oxidative damage (corrosion products) over time, consuming itself as it shields the target structure
